thread:
alex-cs: Heads up — Acme just escalated. After we pushed model v3.2 to a 5% canary, they started seeing tool/function-call failures.

support-jen: Can you paste an example request/response and the request_id?

alex-cs: Here's a redacted example from the customer (they said it worked fine on v3.1):

```json
REQUEST {
  "model": "redwood-model-v3.2",
  "input": "Lookup order 12345",
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "order_lookup",
      "parameters": { "order_id": "12345", "include_items": true }
    }
  ]
}
RESPONSE (returned to customer) {
  "error": {
    "type": "tool_call_schema_validation",
    "message": "missing required property: order_id",
    "tool": "order_lookup_legacy"
  }
}
```

alex-cs: Note: customer says the request body included order_id consistently. They saw the response reference `order_lookup_legacy` even though the tool list only had `order_lookup`.

support-jen: Interesting — looks like tool selection changed. @devon-eng can you pull the routing logs for that request_id?

devon-eng: grabbing logs now. Preliminary: for requests routed to v3.2 in that canary window we're seeing ~11% of function-tool resolutions map to a fallback tool name that only exists on older schemas. Full query: `service=runtime route=canary-v3.2 tool_resolution=true`

lee-runtime: Confirming metrics spike. Tool schema validation errors (% of tool calls that returned schema errors) by model: v3.1 -> 0.7%, v3.2(canary) -> 12.4% across the canary slice. Latency not impacted significantly.

maya-analytics: Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/d/dashboards/toolcall-regressions?org=acme&since=1h — 5-min window at 12:11 shows error rate jump aligned with canary push.

tom-oncall: :warning: If repro looks consistent, recommend pausing the rollout and triggering canary rollback. This is customer-facing failure.

alejandro-ml: Quick theory: v3.2's tokenization/assistant behavior slightly changed how it emits tool names and/or argument ordering; it may be emitting an alternate alias that our router maps to legacy tool. If that alias has different schema, we get validation failures (missing order_id).

devon-eng: I can reproduce locally by running 1000 synthetic calls against v3.2 with the same tool manifest. I see ~9% of responses attempting `order_lookup_legacy` with a payload shape missing nested `parameters.order_id` (looks like it's being flattened/stripped). Sharing repro script in thread.

support-jen: Can we get a sample bad request_id and the customer-facing log? Also need to confirm if auth/billing played any role (customer says not).

canary-bot: Deploy event: pushed model redwood-model-v3.2 to canary (5%) at 2026-03-17T12:10:03Z — artifact: model-v3.2-20260317.

devon-eng: repro request_id: rq_1749901178. Attached runtime trace shows model output: `{"name":"order_lookup_legacy","arguments":"{\"include_items\":true}"}` — arguments string missing order_id.

lee-runtime: That trace matches the schema error in validator. Router did a strict match on tool name; fallback mapping sent to legacy tool.

alex-cs: Customer says impact: ~30 failed order lookups in their workflow (non-critical but blocking some UI flows). They want rollback or mitigation.

tom-oncall: I'll pause the canary rollout now. @devon-eng please open an incident and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml. Also notify the customer and offer temporary pin to v3.1.

devon-eng: Incident created INC-2026-45. Tags: eng-runtime, eng-ml, support. Assigning to @lee-runtime and @alejandro-ml.

alejandro-ml: Plan: 1) Reproduce and isolate whether model emits alternate tool aliases. 2) If model change is causal, coordinate with model owners to patch generation prompt/adapter. 3) Add strict-tool-name canonicalization in router as a short-term mitigation (drop unknown aliases).

lee-runtime: Short-term mitigation: we can block any resolved tool name that ends with `_legacy` for this customer org or globally for the canary slice. That would cause a deterministic failure instead of schema mismatch — which is better UX and easier to trace. I'll implement a hotfix config and push to the canary routing rules.

support-jen: I'll tell Acme we're pausing the canary and offering to pin them to v3.1; asking for any other failing request_ids.

alex-cs: They've accepted pin to v3.1 for now. They provided two more request_ids: rq_1749901189, rq_1749901202.

devon-eng: Thanks — I'll add those to the repro set. Working on a minimal test that reproduces argument-stripping behavior.

maya-analytics: Noting for postmortem: the canary routing policy used randomized user hashing — some tenants received v3.2 earlier; include cohort mapping in incident write-up.

tom-oncall: Update: canary paused at 2026-03-17T12:18Z, rollout halted. Notifying legal/compliance only if data exposure observed (so far none).

alejandro-ml: Early finding: the model's assistant-to-tool adapter prompt changed ordering when a tool had nested params; a small change in generation template caused the assistant to emit a shorthand alias in ~10% cases. We're preparing a model config rollback patch and a stricter adapter enforcement.

devon-eng: Follow-ups: 1) Rollback canary to v3.1 for orgs showing failures; 2) add router canonicalization rule; 3) eng-ml to publish patch and run internal canary. I'll add action items to INC-2026-45.

support-jen: Thanks team. I'll update the customer thread and confirm when their tenant is pinned. :thumbsup:

alex-cs: Customer updated: pin confirmed, they're happy for a follow-up postmortem.

canary-bot: Action: canary roll paused for model redwood-model-v3.2 at 2026-03-17T12:18:09Z (initiated by tom-oncall).

lee-runtime: I'll post logs and the routing hotfix diff to the incident ticket within 30m.

alejandro-ml: ETA for a formal fix and internal canary: 24-36 hours. Will coordinate with runtime for rollout plan.

devon-eng: Closing loop here. If anyone sees another similar org hit, drop request_ids in this thread and we'll add them to the incident.

support-jen: Closing customer update thread; moving discussion to INC-2026-45 for troubleshooting and postmortem.
